contracts.description: loom's write discipline across all three wings: lint-on-write (every mutating call validates the record before commit and rejects malformed input with a typed reason — no silent drop, no torn record), atomic-write parity (every wing gets the atomic-write-with-backup identity already has), and single-writer behavior (concurrent writes are serialized and never interleave; a second concurrent writer to the same store is refused). The concurrency MECHANISM is deliberately unspecified — only the observable behavior (no torn writes, second writer refused) is contract. Forethought / to-be for loom (github.com/jbarket/loom); generalizes the partial discipline already in the knowledge and identity wings.

exclusions: The single-writer MECHANISM: whether loom uses a lockfile, a SQLite advisory lock, a single shared connection, or a write queue is L3's implementation choice — this contract specifies only that writes do not interleave and a second writer is refused, never how.

The exact validation schema per record type beyond 'malformed is rejected with a typed reason': the precise field rules live in each wing's own contract (loom-memory/knowledge/identity); this contract asserts that SOME pre-commit lint runs and rejects, not its full ruleset.
Performance characteristics of serialization (throughput, lock-wait latency): binding, not contract.
goals: TO-BE (forethought): the write discipline (the art-ffc strictness epic) as a cross-cutting contract over all three wings. lint-on-write — every mutating call (remember, knowledge_write, update_identity) validates the record against its shape BEFORE commit and rejects a malformed write with a typed reason, never a silent drop or a torn record. single-writer — concurrent mutation of a store is serialized so writes never interleave, and a second concurrent writer to the same store is refused rather than allowed to corrupt it (BEHAVIOR only; the mechanism — lockfile, advisory lock, single-connection — is L3's to choose).

Some of this exists partially today (knowledge already requires citations and caps bodies; identity already writes atomically with a .bak). This contract GENERALIZES that discipline uniformly and names the gaps (memory's lighter validation, the absence of a concurrency guard, atomic-write parity across wings) as the build list.
Authored before the impl closes the gaps: proposed forethought criteria, no evidence, fixtures define the target.
spec.name: loom-strictness

spec.body: Every mutating call validates its record against the wing's shape BEFORE it commits, and a malformed write is rejected with a typed reason rather than committed-then-broken or silently dropped. This already holds partially in the knowledge wing (a write with zero citations is refused, bodies over cap throw) and the identity wing (the editable-file enum, fence-aware splice); the to-be generalizes it so the MEMORY wing's writes are equally gated, and so EVERY rejection returns a structured reason a caller can act on — no write ever fails silently or half-applies.
spec.title: Lint-on-write — validate before commit, reject with a reason

spec.gherkin:
Given a remember call with a malformed record (e.g. missing required content, or a field of the wrong type)
When it is processed
Then the write is rejected pre-commit with a typed reason and the store is unchanged — memory writes are gated like knowledge writes already are
spec.evidence: src/tools/remember.ts:18-42 (validateMemoryInput rejects empty content/title/category; remember throws the typed reason pre-commit, before createBackend); test src/tools/strictness.test.ts (refuses empty content/title/category, store unchanged via recall).

spec.gherkin:
Given any mutating call that fails validation in any wing
When it is rejected
Then the caller receives a structured reason (what was wrong) and the store is provably unchanged — no write ever fails silently or half-applies
spec.evidence: src/tools/remember.ts:35-42 (typed reason thrown before any backend open); knowledge parity src/tools/knowledge-write.ts:51-58; test src/tools/strictness.test.ts ('a rejected write leaves the store unchanged (no half-apply)').

spec.body: Concurrent mutation of a store is serialized: two writes that arrive together do not interleave into a torn record — each completes wholly or not at all, and the store is never left half-updated. A SECOND concurrent writer to the same store (e.g. a second daemon opening the same memories.db) is refused rather than permitted to race the first into corruption. This is specified as BEHAVIOR — the observable outcomes (serialized, non-interleaved, second-writer-refused) — not as a mechanism; loom may achieve it with a lock, a single connection, or a queue.
spec.title: Single-writer — no torn writes, second writer refused

spec.gherkin:
Given two mutating calls to the same store arriving concurrently
When both are processed
Then their effects are serialized — the resulting records are each whole (no interleaving), and the store reflects both writes applied in some order, never a torn merge
spec.evidence: better-sqlite3 is synchronous and each write is wrapped in db.transaction() (src/backends/sqlite-vec.ts:122-138), so concurrent calls cannot interleave; test src/tools/strictness.test.ts ('serializes concurrent writes — both records land whole').

spec.gherkin:
Given a store already held by one writer and a second concurrent writer attempting to open the same store
When the second writer starts
Then it is refused (not allowed to race the first into corruption) — the observable single-writer guarantee, however the implementation enforces it
spec.evidence: WAL admits one writer; busy_timeout=0 makes a second concurrent writer fail fast (src/backends/sqlite-vec.ts:89-96, src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts:62-66); test src/tools/strictness.test.ts ('refuses a second concurrent writer (fail-fast, no block)').

spec.body: The atomic-write-with-backup discipline the identity wing already has (copy prior content to .bak, then tmp-write + rename, so a crash mid-write never truncates) extends to every wing's durable writes. A crash or kill in the middle of any commit leaves either the prior state or the new state intact, never a truncated or partial store. Identity has this today; the to-be brings memory and knowledge to parity.
spec.title: Atomic-write parity — every wing crash-safe

spec.item: Every wing's durable writes are atomic with a backup: a crash or kill mid-commit leaves either the prior state or the new state, never a truncated store. A conforming implementation routes memory and knowledge commits through the same atomic-write-with-backup discipline the identity wing already uses (copy-to-.bak, tmp-write, rename) — crash-safety is uniform across the three stores, not identity-only.
spec.evidence: DB wings are crash-safe via WAL + db.transaction() ACID (src/backends/sqlite-vec.ts:89,122; src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts:62); identity via atomicWriteWithBackup (src/path-safety.ts:57-66); test src/tools/strictness.test.ts ('a rejected write leaves the store unchanged').

spec.description: Witness: a kill mid-commit leaves prior-or-new, never truncated.
A malformed remember is rejected pre-commit; store unchanged.
A rejected write leaves the store provably unchanged (no half-apply).
A failed validation returns a structured reason.
A second concurrent writer to the same store is refused.
Two concurrent writes serialize; neither record is torn.
